task_type: production navigation incident repair and controlled release
requested_outcome: Prevent the public events page and other primary worlds from falling into a terminal error during navigation or a release transition, reduce the events landing critical path, publish once, and verify the exact live release
natural_destination: https://vii.spaplus.co/events and shared primary-world navigation on vii.spaplus.co
authorization_boundary: Diagnosis, local repair, regression tests, one controlled public publication and live verification are authorized; destructive data, DNS, permission and environment changes are excluded

lesson_bundle.reason: The incident is on VII shared navigation and the events world
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Use the VII master plan and feedback standard as product truth

lesson_bundle.reason: The previous approval missed a live navigation state
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require exact public navigation, reload, recovery and affected-family evidence

lesson_bundle.reason: The repair crosses a managed public release boundary
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Freeze one source, preserve rollback and verify the exact deployed identity

predicted_rejections.rejection: A direct refresh works but client-side navigation still reaches the old terminal error
predicted_rejections.prevention: Test both direct document loads and same-origin RSC navigation, including a simulated generation mismatch
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The mismatch performs one GET document replacement and matching-generation navigation remains seamless

predicted_rejections.rejection: Events is repaired while another world using the same global fetch path breaks
predicted_rejections.prevention: Treat events, spas, hourly and vacations as the affected navigation family
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: All primary world routes pass the shared generation-boundary test and live navigation checks

predicted_rejections.rejection: The page remains so slow that users interpret it as broken or trigger a timeout
predicted_rejections.prevention: Remove live full-catalog D1 work from the events landing critical path and deduplicate its editorial read
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The exact public events route returns complete content without the terminal boundary and improves against the 3.9 to 6.4 second baseline

predicted_rejections.rejection: A recovery loop or duplicated action creates a worse failure
predicted_rejections.prevention: Limit recovery to same-origin GET RSC responses, guard once per build pair and never replay POST or API actions
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Negative tests prove actions, external requests and repeated mismatches are not replayed

affected_family: events landing document and RSC render
events, spas, hourly and vacations primary-world routes

sources.label: Observed public failure
sources.source: user screenshot of the public /events terminal error on 2026-11-12

midpoint_gate.trigger: After the focused release-generation tests and before the full build and publication
checks: mismatched-generation RSC replaces the exact document once
events uses the accepted build-local catalog on the landing critical path
POST, external and repeated requests are not replayed

attack_questions: Can a tab opened before publication navigate to events after publication without a terminal boundary?
Can repeated events reloads produce a 500, blank page or old error copy?
Can the shared recovery replay a POST, external request or loop?
Can desktop pass while a 390 pixel mobile navigation fails?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Exact public /events direct load, home-to-events navigation, reload and back/forward evidence on the deployed build
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Focused tests plus live desktop and mobile traversal across events, spas, hourly and vacations

effectiveness.baseline: Public /events direct GETs took 3.9 to 6.4 seconds and an already-open client displayed the old terminal route boundary during navigation
effectiveness.target: No terminal boundary in the representative navigation matrix, one publication, and materially lower /events response latency
